titulo: What If You Fell Into the Grand Canyon? Movies vs Reality #shorts
premisa: You slip at a Grand Canyon overlook. The video shows the fall you have seen in movies, then corrects each part. MOVIE: you drop a full mile in a straight line. REALITY: the deepest point is about a mile down (roughly 6,000 feet), and a fall that long would take around 20 seconds, hitting about 120 mph after roughly 12. MOVIE: the bottom is a cool river. REALITY: the inner canyon runs about 20°F hotter than the rim, and summer days at Phantom Ranch often pass 110°F. With no shade and no water, the heat becomes a second enemy. MOVIE: a helicopter scoops you up for free. REALITY: park rangers run rescues hundreds of times a year, but an air ambulance flight to a hospital can cost tens of thousands of dollars. Narration stays short and punchy, with tension building at each 'reality' beat until the twist.
gancho: What if you fell into the Grand Canyon? Forget the movies. Here's what really happens.
